BUILD THE CONTROL PROGRAM

Your PLC

Add rungs to control the floor.

Instructions, tags, and this floor's requirements

Deliver six parts. All actuator commands must switch off when RUN is off, READY is off, or FAULT is on. The test exercises these conditions on a fresh simulation.

Series contacts mean AND. Contacts inside a parallel group mean OR. A ! prefix is an XIO contact: true when its bit is off. OTE follows the rung, OTL latches a bit, and OTU unlatches it. Use M1 to M16 for memory. TON and RTO use T1 to T8; CTU uses C1 to C8; RES resets a timer or counter. Use T1_DONE or C1_DONE as contacts.

Q_A drives station A. S_A is its occupancy photoeye, CLEAR_A reports space at the requested destination, and FAULT_A reports its fault. Apply the same naming to other stations.

Stops require Q plus RELEASE. Lifts require your UP and DOWN commands to reach the upper limit and return to the lower limit before Q can transfer a box. UPPER, LOWER, and CYCLED bits report the lift state; CYCLED resets when the box leaves. Opposing lift commands fail the test.

At a branch, WANT_A_B means the part's work order requests B next. Your PLC must select exactly the matching ROUTE_A_B output. Work orders define destinations, not actuator commands. Only energize routing outputs when that request is present. Wrong or simultaneous routes fail.

Example contact arrangement: RUN AND READY AND !FAULT. Add your station conditions and choose the required output. No solution is loaded for you.

How to practice

Add rungs below the diagram, then run or step through your program. Each floor saves its own draft in this browser. Reset simulation clears machine state but keeps your program. Editing a rung pauses and resets the machine so stale outputs cannot keep it moving.

This is a discrete training simulation. Transport spacing and merge reservations are enforced by the plant model. Successful tests demonstrate the listed objectives, not industrial safety certification.
